message: I was denied a collect call from an inmate in Texas and discovered that T-Netix had blocked the call. I was contacted the next day by an automated system that would quide me through to a rep that would take my very personal information. It seems if ones credit rating is not just right they can decline service to you or ask for a greater deposit.  During my years in Texas I worked for the PRISON WORKERS UNION, (a bunch of volunteers with the ACLU) and got to know a lot of caring families and the inmates that belonged to them. Most of these families can not put up that kind of money at once. Correctional billing holds these families hostage with the love they have for someone that happens to be incacerated paying for that alleged crime. How much more has to be paid?  From my research a lot of the revenue these companies brag of are coming from the pockets of those least able to spare it. The prison systems in this nation are well networked through family support groups and even more through the inmates themselves. What would happen if all the phones went silent for just a month and we picked up our pens and paper instead. Boycotts are not a difficult action to put together. I am planting seed all over the net. Let me know what your thoughts are.
